plan.vision: A strict Spec Roadmap detailing the exact Agentic problem, atomic milestones, and Testing Strategy. The project aims to provide a lightweight, efficient, and secure tool for developers to enhance their coding flow by automating repetitive tasks, such as code formatting, linting, and running tests. The agent will be designed to work seamlessly with existing development environments and will support cross-platform functionality.
plan.lessons_learned: This project avoids past mistakes by using memory-mapped files for efficient data handling, prioritizing algorithmic efficiency over OOP overhead, and ensuring that all dependencies are pinned in a virtual environment. The repository will be kept lightweight by excluding heavy directories with .gitignore, and clear setup scripts will be provided for reproducibility. Additionally, the project will focus on security and isolation, ensuring that the code executed within the sandbox cannot access or modify external resources. There are no hidden paid-API dependencies.
plan.commit_message: Implement a lightweight, efficient, and secure CodeFlowAgent to automate repetitive coding tasks.

files_to_generate.instructions: Contains the core logic for the CodeFlowAgent. This file should include functions for formatting code, linting code, and running tests. Use pure functions and dependency injection to decouple core logic from side-effects.
Handles configuration management. Include a ConfigManager class with methods to load and save configurations. Ensure that the configuration is loaded and saved securely.

Provides utility functions for reading and writing files. Functions should handle file I/O operations and return appropriate results. Ensure that these functions are robust and handle errors gracefully.
Includes a strict unit test suite for the CodeFlowAgent. Import and use the actual generated modules. Do not create mock or stub classes for the core logic. The code must pass its own tests.
Ignore venv, __pycache__, .env, and other non-essential files and directories. Ensure that the repository remains lightweight and clean.
Explains the architecture of the project, how to set up the environment, and how to run the tests. Provide clear instructions and examples to help users understand and use the CodeFlowAgent.
A setup script to install the necessary dependencies and set up the virtual environment. Pin all dependencies to specific versions to ensure reproducibility.
List all the required Python packages and their specific versions. Ensure that the dependencies are lightweight and do not include heavy ML libraries.
